findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. The intent is admin OR owner. `isTeamAdmin` already returns true for both roles, so the `&&` effectively requires an owner and a plain team ADMIN is denied. Those admins get FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The condition should be `||`, or just `isTeamAdmin`. The route also uses `authedProcedure`, not the `bookingsProcedure` that `editLocation` uses, so this hand-rolled check is the only authorization.

findings.title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, and the input is not deduplicated server-side
findings.body: The blacklist is lower-cased, but each `guest` is compared as-is. `Blocked@Example.com` therefore bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The existing-attendee check `guest === attendee.email` is also case-sensitive, so the same address in a different case is added as a second attendee. Duplicate entries within `guests` are only rejected by the client dialog. A direct tRPC call with the same email twice creates two attendee rows, because `uniqueGuests` never dedupes the input. Lower-case the emails and dedupe on the server.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw `guests` list instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: The emails are sent with `guests`, the unfiltered request input, not `uniqueGuests`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide between the full 'scheduled' email and the 'guests added' notification. If the request includes an address that is already an attendee, that existing attendee is wrongly sent a fresh 'scheduled' invite instead of the update notice. Pass the list of guests that were actually inserted.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before the calendar update with no error handling or rollback
findings.body: The DB update that creates the attendees runs first. `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` follows with no try/catch. If the calendar update throws, the client sees an error but the guests are already stored and no emails are sent. A retry then filters those guests out as duplicates and fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, so the user cannot complete the operation. The calendar and DB state are left inconsistent. Handle calendar failures explicitly, or reorder the steps and roll back.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials rather than the organizer's
findings.body: `EventManager` is built from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `...user`. The route also permits attendees and team admins to add guests. For those callers the credentials do not belong to the user whose calendar holds the event, so `updateCalendarAttendees` will fail or silently skip the external event. The organizer's calendar (`booking.user`, which is already loaded with its credentials) is the one that should be updated.

findings.title: Any attendee can add an unbounded number of arbitrary guests, which sends emails to arbitrary addresses
findings.body: Any logged-in user whose email matches an attendee of the booking is authorized. Neither `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` nor the handler limits the array size, and the booking status is not checked. A single call with many addresses triggers organizer, team and per-attendee emails and ICS invites to third parties, which makes it a spam vector. The attendee check is also case-sensitive on `user.email`. Add a max count, tighten who may add guests, and consider rejecting cancelled/rejected bookings.

findings.title: CalendarEvent has no `team`, so the team-member email loop in sendAddGuestsEmails never runs
findings.body: `evt` is built without `team` or any team member info, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` iterates `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify the other hosts. For collective and round-robin team events that loop is dead code, and the other hosts are never told about the new guests. The subject also falls back to the organizer's name instead of the team name. Other fields such as `responses` and `bookerUrl` are missing too, which can degrade the email content.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other send function takes `eventTypeMetadata` and honors `disableStandardEmails.all.host` and `.attendee`. `sendAddGuestsEmails` has no such parameter and always sends host and attendee emails. Event types that disabled standard emails (e.g. for workflow-only or custom notifications) will still send these messages to hosts, existing attendees and the new guests.

findings.title: Case-sensitive match on new guest email
findings.body: `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` compares strings exactly. The attendee emails come from the DB and the guest list from user input, so a casing difference sends a new guest the 'guests added' notification instead of the full scheduled invite.

findings.title: isInvalidEmail is never cleared on success or on dialog dismiss
findings.body: `isInvalidEmail` is set when validation fails and is only reset by the Cancel button. If the user triggers the error, corrects the emails and submits successfully, `onSuccess` resets the values but not the flag. The error banner then reappears the next time the dialog opens. Closing the dialog via overlay or Esc (`onOpenChange`) also keeps stale emails and error state.

findings.title: Error toast is always prefixed with the code and the fallback message is unreachable
findings.body: `message` is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`, which is always a non-empty string. `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` can therefore never run, and users see raw text like `BAD_REQUEST: Emails must be unique and valid` or `undefined: ...`. The new `unable_to_add_guests` string is dead. Also, `handleAdd` silently returns when the email list is empty.

findings.title: Hardcoded English tooltip and a label not bound to an input
findings.body: The tooltip `"Remove email"` is not passed through `t()`, unlike the rest of the component. The `<label htmlFor="emails">` references an id that no input has, so the label is not associated with the fields. Rows use `key={index}`, which is fragile when entries are removed from the middle of the list.

findings.title: Email failures are swallowed without logging the error
findings.body: The catch block only logs a fixed string with `console.log` and drops `err`. If sending fails, the user still gets a 'Guests added' success and operators have nothing to diagnose it. At minimum log the error through the project logger.

findings.title: Blacklisted or duplicate guests are silently dropped and the all-filtered error is misleading
findings.body: If only some of the submitted guests are filtered out (existing attendee or blacklisted), the request still succeeds and the UI shows 'Guests added', with no indication that some were skipped. If all are filtered, the user gets 'Emails must be unique and valid' even when the cause is the blacklist. The response should report what was actually added or skipped.

findings.title: New feature ships without any tests
findings.body: The PR adds a mutation with non-trivial authorization, filtering and email logic, plus new UI and email templates, but no handler unit tests or e2e tests. The `data-testid="add_members"` hook is added but never exercised. Bugs like the `&&` permission check and the wrong `newGuests` list would be caught by basic tests.
